A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 18-page versions of the AnySat paper. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original GeoPlex and external-dataset evaluations, fine-tuning and probing results, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices A-B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds SpaceNet7 results and further foundation-model comparisons in Table 1.

M1.justification: The scale-adaptive encoder, modality combiner, JEPA and contrastive objectives, masking, and downstream adaptation procedures in Section 3 and Appendix C are retained. No algorithm or architecture change is documented.

E1.justification: Table 1 adds SpaceNet7 evaluation using Planet imagery, marked as an unseen sensor. The five GeoPlex datasets and six previously evaluated external datasets remain; the GeoBench/PANGAEA framing largely regroups existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 substantially expands comparator sets for retained tasks. HLS and flood comparisons gain ScaleMAE, RemoteCLIP, and DINO-S12; PASTIS-HD segmentation gains comparisons with CROMA, DOFA, and SatlasNet, among others. DINO-S12 matches the earlier S12-DINO, and existing appendix comparators remain.

E3.justification: Table 1 adds SpaceNet7 fine-tuning/probing and a Fold1-specific PASTIS-HD fine-tuning comparison alongside existing results. Its So2Sat probing budget is labeled 6K versus 29K in v2, but v3 Table B retains 29K; an actual configuration change is therefore unconfirmed.

E4.justification: The random-dropping, contrastive-loss, and subpatch-segmentation ablations are unchanged in the renumbered Table 2. Appendix B's modality/temporal-masking experiment and Figure B's qualitative examples are also retained. The new table adds benchmark comparisons rather than a distinct supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed/run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new table continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially expands numerical comparisons, including new SpaceNet7 scores of 58.8/58.1 mIoU for AnySat fine-tuning/probing, PASTIS-HD Fold1 fine-tuning at 65.9 mIoU, and numerous additional baseline scores. Existing appendix scores remain. Prithvi2's flood score is newly listed as 89.9, conflicting with 90.4 retained in Table B; no correction or setting difference is explained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, losses in Equations 1-5, and scale-adaptive positional encoding in Appendix Equation A are unchanged. No proof or formal assumption is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified heterogeneous EO pretraining, sensor adaptability, and downstream performance. The additional benchmark evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Explanations of pretraining benefits, dense-supervision effects, masking tradeoffs, and limits on unseen-sensor probing are retained. The added resizing/sliding-window note specifies comparison procedures without introducing a distinct causal argument or limitation.

D1.justification: Table 1 discloses additional trainable-parameter budgets, including 3M for SpaceNet7 probing and 33K for PASTIS-HD probing. Section 4.2 adds specific baseline resizing/sliding-window information. Existing implementation, hardware, and code/model access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Adds references to Geo-Bench, PANGAEA, RemoteCLIP, and USat while retaining the related-work narrative and novelty positioning. USat is cited by Table 1's SatlasNet row; this citation mismatch does not establish USat as an additional evaluated comparator.

P1.justification: Section 4.2 gains a short benchmark-comparison passage, with corresponding citation and table-reference updates. The abstract, method exposition, conclusion, and appendix narrative remain essentially unchanged, without broad rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: Adds a full-width Table 1 with fine-tuning/probing columns, parameter budgets, and sensor-status coloring, partly redisplaying appendix results. The ablation table becomes Table 2 and moves to page 9; Table B rows are reordered. Existing figures remain unchanged apart from citation numbers.

improvement.justification: The broader foundation-model comparisons and additional unseen-sensor evaluation provide useful evidence for the central versatility claim and make parameter-efficiency tradeoffs easier to inspect. This modest benefit is limited by sparse SpaceNet7 protocol documentation and introduced inconsistencies: Prithvi2's flood score is 89.9 versus 90.4 in Table B, and So2Sat probing is labeled 6K versus 29K. The core method and previous supporting analyses remain intact.
